title: Still Waters, Rapid Currents: Early Labor Market Transformation under Generative AI (NBER Working Paper 33777; previously circulated as 'Large Language Models, Small Labor Market Effects')
authors_or_organization: Anders Humlum; Emilie Vestergaard (University of Chicago / NBER)
data_collection_dates: Surveys in 2023 and late 2024 (about 25,000 complete responses per round; 11 exposed occupations, ~7,000 workplaces), linked to Danish administrative registers
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Center for Applied Artificial Intelligence and Polsky Center (Chicago Booth); not peer reviewed (NBER WP)
limitations: Time savings, new tasks and reallocation are self-reported; employer initiatives are worker-perceived; new-task categories derived from free-text coding; Danish labor market; covers general chatbots, not outside-advisor deliverables. The version read is the March 2026 revision (title changed); figures may differ from the May 2025 version.

title: The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking: Self-Reported Reductions in Cognitive Effort and Confidence Effects From a Survey of Knowledge Workers (CHI '25)
authors_or_organization: Hao-Ping (Hank) Lee (CMU); Advait Sarkar; Lev Tankelevitch; Ian Drosos; Sean Rintel; Richard Banks; Nicholas Wilson (Microsoft Research)
data_collection_dates: not reported in extracted text (online Prolific survey)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Six of seven authors are Microsoft Research employees (Microsoft sells GenAI tools)
limitations: Cross-sectional peer-reviewed survey study, not an experiment; n=319 Prolific knowledge workers, 936 self-reported examples; perceived effort, not measured time or accuracy; sample skewed younger/tech-oriented per authors; correlational betas.

title: The hidden cost of AI 'workslop' — and how leaders can fix it (BetterUp blog; with Stanford Social Media Lab)
authors_or_organization: BetterUp Labs (in partnership with Stanford Social Media Lab)
data_collection_dates: September 2025 (online survey; text says 1,004 full-time US desk workers, footnote/infographic says 1,150)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: BetterUp is a commercial coaching company; survey run by BetterUp with an academic partner
limitations: Blog summary of a survey; no questionnaire, sampling frame or response rate published in the post; inconsistent N (1,004 vs 1,150); self-reported time per instance and self-estimated share of content; cost figures not reproducible from stated numbers; 'workslop' defined by recipients' perceptions.

title: AI-Generated 'Workslop' Is Destroying Productivity (Harvard Business Review)
authors_or_organization: Kate Niederhoffer; Gabriella Rosen Kellerman; Angela Lee; Alex Liebscher; Kristina Rapuano; Jeffrey T. Hancock
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Authors affiliated with BetterUp Labs and Stanford Social Media Lab
limitations: Only the header and summary were retrievable (paywall); no evidence items drawn directly from this source; listed to anchor the evidence group. Same underlying survey as WS5-S03.

title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Evaluation (Department for Business and Trade)
authors_or_organization: UK Department for Business and Trade (DBT), Digital Data and Technology Monitoring and Evaluation team
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Buyer-authored internal evaluation of a licensed vendor product; no vendor funding reported
limitations: Theory-based evaluation without a counterfactual for diary data; diary response rate 32%; self-reported time savings with estimated counterfactual time; observed tasks have very small samples (exact n per task not reported in extracted text); government policy setting, not investment decisions; Copilot generation of late 2024.

title: Evaluation of a trial of generative artificial intelligence (Copilot) in the Department of the Treasury
authors_or_organization: Australian Centre for Evaluation (ACE), Australian Government Department of the Treasury
data_collection_dates: Trial 20 May-23 August 2024 (14 weeks), 218 participating staff
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Buyer-authored internal evaluation; no vendor funding reported
limitations: Volunteer participants; surveys, focus groups, case studies and issues log; time savings not explicitly measured; protected security environment restricted functionality; policy-department setting.

title: Spotlight: Staff Update on Outreach Activities Related to the Integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Audits and Financial Reporting
data_collection_dates: not reported (outreach prior to July 2024 with U.S. global network firms and several non-affiliated firms auditing >100 issuers, plus preparers)
limitations: Staff views, not Board rules; describes what firms told the regulator (stated policies), not observed practice or measured time; 'some firms' quantifiers unspecified; early-stage adoption.

title: The state of board reporting (Board Intelligence blog; with Chartered Governance Institute UK & Ireland)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Board Intelligence sells board-reporting software (Report Writer) that addresses the problems reported
limitations: Vendor self-assessment tool data, self-selected respondents, N not stated; page read via automated extraction (inconsistent average-length figures 226 vs 220 pages on the page); no measure of preparation or reformatting time.

title: Directors Want Less Volume, More Insight: Key Findings (Society for Corporate Governance blog summarizing a Society/Board Intelligence report)
authors_or_organization: Society for Corporate Governance (Randi Morrison blog); report with Board Intelligence
data_collection_dates: not reported (five Society member surveys, two roundtables, interviews)
limitations: Blog summary only; underlying report not retrieved; sample sizes not stated; governance professionals (preparers) rather than directors; no preparation-time data.

title: A&O announces exclusive launch partnership with Harvey
data_collection_dates: Beta trial from November 2022 to announcement
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Buyer announcement of an exclusive launch partnership with the vendor (commercial relationship)
limitations: Promotional announcement; usage counts self-reported; no time-savings, error, or review-effort data.

title: AI in practice at Moonfare
authors_or_organization: Philip Meschke, Head of Private Equity, Moonfare
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Moonfare is a private-markets investment platform; post has marketing function
limitations: Buyer-authored blog; time figures unmeasured/anecdotal and partly forward-looking estimates; no description of review steps; about this one firm.

title: AI-Driven Investment Memo Acceleration for a PE Secondary Transaction (case study)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Vendor marketing for its own product
limitations: Anonymous client; no measurement method; no description of who reviewed outputs or how; selection of a favorable case; read via automated page extraction.

title: Appendix D: Preliminary Due Diligence List (Developmental Solar Resources), 3 GW Alternative Market-Based Mechanism Process RFP for Solar Photovoltaic Resources for Entergy Louisiana, LLC
url: https://rfp.entergy.com/ENTRFP/SEND/ELL3GWSOLARRFP/Documents/Appendix D Due Diligence List - Developmental Solar.pdf
limitations: Utility procurement of developer bids (buyer = offtaker/owner), not an investor engaging an advisor; shows stated requirements, not how they are used or how much review effort they save.

title: Do Management Interventions Last? Evidence from India (NBER WP 24249; published AEJ: Applied Economics 2020)
authors_or_organization: Nicholas Bloom; Aprajit Mahajan; David McKenzie; John Roberts
funding_or_commercial_relationships: SEED (Stanford GSB) and World Bank Strategic Research Program
limitations: Small number of firms (Indian textile weaving, multi-plant family firms); operational management practices, not analytical deliverables; reasons for dropping practices are directors'/managers' stated reasons; WP version read, not final AEJ version.

title: Overcoming Algorithm Aversion: People Will Use (Imperfect) Algorithms If They Can (Even Slightly) Modify Them (Management Science 64(3):1155-1170, 2018)
authors_or_organization: Berkeley J. Dietvorst; Joseph P. Simmons; Cade Massey (Wharton)
limitations: Pre-publication version on author's institutional site (title differs slightly from published); incentivized lab/online forecasting of student test percentiles by lay participants; algorithm, not human advisor; small stakes.
